review_notes: I read the whole target file (lines 1–415) and inspected candidate Mathlib sources for each family of declarations: real/NNReal/ENNReal limit lemmas (`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Continuity.lean`, `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/ENNRealLogExp.lean`, `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Exp.lean`, `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean`), the `IsBigO`/`IsLittleO`/`IsTheta` API (`Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/*`), complex `cpow` comparisons (`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/CompareExp.lean`), and Gaussian/Polynomial/Mellin users of the rpow–exp lemmas. I grepped for `rpow`, `tendsto_rpow`, `isLittleO_rpow_exp`, `rpow_rpow_nhdsGE_zero`, `IsBigO.rpow`, `sqrt` asymptotics and `log_rpow_rpow`; no other declaration in Mathlib (outside this file and its users) states the same specific concepts as the target's `tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop`, `tendsto_rpow_neg_nhdsGT_zero`, the four `tendsto_rpow_*_of_base_*` lemmas, `tendsto_exp_div_rpow_atTop`, `tendsto_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_atTop_nhds_zero`, the `IsBigOWith/IsBigO/IsTheta/IsLittleO.rpow` and `.sqrt` extensions, the `nhdsGE` rpow comparisons, or the log–rpow asymptotics. Near misses I deliberately abstained on: (1) `tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_lt_one` and `ENNReal.tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_lt_one` share a name but live on different carriers (ℝ vs ℝ≥0∞) and the real version explicitly handles negative bases via `Real.rpow_def_of_nonpos`, so they are not the same concept; the shared name is a naming-convention question, not the rubric's duplication concept. (2) `isLittleO_rpow_exp_atTop` / `isLittleO_pow_exp_pos_mul_atTop` are more general than `Real.isLittleO_pow_exp_atTop` in `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Exp.lean`, i.e. the existing lemma is a specialisation, not a replacement. (3) The `IsBigO.sqrt`/`IsLittleO.sqrt`/`IsTheta.sqrt` lemmas are named API obtained via `rpow`, which the rubric explicitly says is not redundancy. (4) `tendsto_rpow_div` and `tendsto_rpow_neg_div` are thin named corollaries of `tendsto_rpow_div_mul_add` in the same file; named specialisations are not defects. Limitation: I could not compile anything, so I did not test whether e.g. the Real base-change lemmas could be derived from an ENNReal statement by coercion; the type-level differences and the negative-base case make that unclear, and the rubric says to abstain when the practical case for consolidation is unclear.
